page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m4.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for high-concurrency enterprise environments. Powered by the KVM hypervisor on the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 64 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.25 GHz. The system provides 256.0 GB of total memory, establishing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM distribution with 4.0 GB allocated per core. The instance operates entirely without hardware graphics accelerators, containing zero GPUs.

Storage and networking configurations reflect a decoupled architecture. The ecs.u2a-c1m4.16xlarge features no local storage, requiring all operating system and persistent data volumes to be hosted on remote network-attached block storage. Network performance is anchored by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth, providing steady throughput for inter-node communication and remote storage access. The server includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual private cloud routing and elastic IP provisioning for external connectivity.

The qualitative resource efficiency of this instance stems from its high density of dedicated cores and uniform memory distribution. While the absence of local NVMe storage limits ultra-low-latency local disk caching, it simplifies instance state management and volume failover across host nodes. The ecs.u2a-c1m4.16xlarge is suited for scalable enterprise software, multi-tiered web application backends, mid-tier relational databases utilizing networked block storage, container cluster worker nodes, and data processing pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u2a-c1m4.16xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 64 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.25 GHz and 256.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 ratio with 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, relying on network-attached block storage for all operational and persistent disk needs. Network capabilities are supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while public networking requires external IP allocation due to the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Delivering consistent, dedicated compute density without shared-core interference, this server fits large-scale application serving, containerized workloads, enterprise business software, and distributed data processing tiers.
